learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears.

items.title: Starting check: identify modeling
items.prompt: A child watches an adult sort recycling by label and later uses the same sorting rule without direct instruction. Which process is most directly shown?

items.title: Guided practice: separate learning and performance
items.prompt: An observer accurately describes a demonstrated procedure but does not perform it until equipment becomes available. Which statement fits?

items.title: Less help: identify vicarious emotion
items.prompt: A viewer tenses while watching another person approach a visibly painful obstacle. Which process is most directly illustrated?

items.title: Solo practice: bound neural evidence
items.prompt: Brain activity overlaps during action observation and action execution. Which conclusion is appropriately bounded?
options: One neuron system explains all empathy

items.title: Near exit: trace the chain
items.prompt: A trainee watches a model receive praise for checking a safety seal and later adds that check. Which explanation is best?
options: Praise directly altered the trainee’s genes

items.title: Changed exit: integrate vicarious evidence
items.prompt: An observer reports fear while viewing another person’s distress, and an action-emotion network is active. Which claim is best bounded?
options: The network alone caused all fear

items.title: Repair: name visible information
items.prompt: A novice sees a model use a checklist and avoid an error. What information is available to the observer?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: explain a new model
items.prompt: A new employee watches a coworker calm a customer with a brief summary and later uses that technique. Which process fits?

items.title: Repair: avoid a single mechanism
items.prompt: Which statement best handles mirror-neuron evidence in an observational-learning case?
options: It proves all learning is neural mimicry

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A viewer mirrors another’s expression and reports a similar emotion. Which conclusion stays within introductory depth?
options: One brain region fully explains emotion
The viewer learned every model behavior

items.title: Starting check: use observed reward
items.prompt: A student sees a similar peer praised for showing work and can use the same method. What is the most bounded prediction?
options: Showing work may become more likely

items.title: Guided practice: use observed cost
items.prompt: An employee watches a coworker ignore a safety step and receive a formal penalty. Which prediction is most direct?
options: The observer cannot learn the action

items.title: Less help: use model relevance
items.prompt: Two models demonstrate a technique. One shares the observer’s experience level and succeeds. Which effect is plausible?
options: The other model cannot be observed
Experience level has no possible role

items.title: Solo practice: distinguish learning from ability
items.prompt: An observer watches a skilled gymnast complete a move but lacks the strength to reproduce it. Which statement fits?

items.title: Near exit: combine the four gates
items.prompt: A credible model receives a reward for a simple behavior the observer can perform tomorrow. Which prediction is best?
options: The behavior may become more likely
The reward has no social meaning

items.title: Changed exit: alter the consequence
items.prompt: A model previously rewarded for speaking up is now repeatedly penalized for it. What change is most directly predicted?
options: The observer forgets the behavior instantly

items.title: Repair: fill the prediction gates
items.prompt: A relevant model is rewarded, but the observer has no chance to perform the action. Which statement is best?
options: Reward removes the need for ability

items.title: Fresh re-entry: predict a new behavior
items.prompt: A novice sees a respected peer rewarded for using a planning checklist and soon faces the same task. Which outcome is plausible?

items.title: Repair: alter capability only
items.prompt: An observer values a rewarded behavior but loses the equipment required to perform it. What changes first?

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A model’s behavior shifts from praised to publicly criticized while observer ability stays constant. Which prediction is bounded?

items.title: Starting check: identify central processing
items.prompt: A highly involved audience has time and knowledge to compare evidence quality in a message. Which ELM route is most likely?

items.title: Guided practice: identify cue sensitivity
items.prompt: A distracted audience has little personal stake and responds mainly to a familiar spokesperson. Which prediction fits ELM?

items.title: Less help: select social cognitive theory
items.prompt: A person watches a similar peer succeed, reports higher confidence, and begins practicing in an accessible setting. Which model best organizes the case?

items.title: Solo practice: use reciprocal influence
items.prompt: Practice improves skill, improved skill raises confidence, and confidence increases later practice. Which concept fits?

items.title: Near exit: select the model
items.prompt: A study varies argument strength and audience involvement while holding the behavioral setting constant. Which model is most directly tested?

items.title: Changed exit: alter ability to elaborate
items.prompt: Two groups receive strong arguments and care equally, but one group is heavily distracted. What does ELM predict?

items.title: Repair: map the changed variable
items.prompt: A case changes source attractiveness while audience motivation remains low. Which model component is most direct?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: choose a new model
items.prompt: A person sees a peer succeed, gains confidence, and practices more because equipment is available. Which model fits?

items.title: Repair: contrast the predictions
items.prompt: Which change most directly raises central-route processing in ELM?
options: Lower confidence in a physical skill

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new intervention leaves arguments unchanged but increases confidence and practice access. Which theory predicts more behavior?

items.title: Starting check: classify a message factor
items.prompt: A study changes argument evidence while keeping audience and social setting constant. Which factor class changed?

items.title: Guided practice: classify a target factor
items.prompt: The same message produces more change among people who consider the issue personally important. Which factor class differs?

items.title: Less help: classify a social factor
items.prompt: Attitudes shift after participants learn that their valued peer group approves the position. Which class is most direct?

items.title: Solo practice: classify behavior
items.prompt: Participants first sign a public statement and later report attitudes more consistent with that action. Which factor class changed first?

items.title: Near exit: predict from one class
items.prompt: A strong argument replaces a weak argument while target motivation and social context stay constant. Which prediction is most bounded?

items.title: Changed exit: interpret an interaction
items.prompt: Strong arguments outperform weak ones only among highly involved targets; low-involvement targets show no difference. Which conclusion fits?
options: Strong arguments work equally for everyone

items.title: Repair: use the four boxes
items.prompt: A message is unchanged, but recipients differ in prior knowledge. Which box receives the changed variable?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify a new factor
items.prompt: A new study holds the message constant and varies whether close friends endorse it. Which class changed?

items.title: Repair: compare within each level
items.prompt: A graph shows source credibility matters only when targets have low prior knowledge. Which statement captures the interaction?

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new graph shows a public commitment changes attitudes more under supportive group norms than neutral norms. Which conclusion is bounded?
options: Commitment has the same effect everywhere
